bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory risk — Changes in regulatory requirements and compliance frameworks could impact operations and product approvals. The BRSR material-issues table also flags Regulatory Compliance as a risk with negative financial implications, noting the business 'can be influenced by frequent and intricate regulatory changes'. Mitigation is stated as strong regulatory compliance programmes and quality assurance systems aligned with global regulatory standards, plus active monitoring of amendments to rules, regulations and laws.
- Competition and pricing risk — The pharmaceutical industry is described as highly competitive, with pricing pressure, product innovation cycles and new market entrants intensifying competition. The MD&A separately lists pricing pressures in generic markets and increasing competition among the conditions that may continue to influence operating performance. Mitigation is a focus on differentiated products and complex injectables plus sustained R&D investment and partnerships with global pharmaceutical companies.
- Supply chain risk — Disruptions in raw material sourcing, logistics challenges or geopolitical developments may impact product availability and delivery timelines; the MD&A also cites fluctuations in raw material and energy costs. Mitigation is supplier-base diversification, stronger procurement monitoring and strategic inventory buffers.
- Financial and market risk — Financial performance may be affected by market volatility, pricing pressures and operational inefficiencies; the MD&A additionally cites foreign exchange volatility. Mitigation is a diversified product portfolio, a strong balance sheet, strategic cost management and operational efficiency initiatives.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk — Cybersecurity threats, data breaches and IT disruptions could impact operational continuity and data integrity. Mitigation is leading-edge cybersecurity systems, robust IT governance, regular vulnerability assessments and employee awareness programmes.
- Human resource / key-talent risk — Attracting and retaining skilled professionals remains critical for sustaining operational excellence and innovation. Permanent-employee turnover was 14% in FY 2026 (14% in FY 2025 and 23% in FY 2024). Mitigation is talent development initiatives, leadership programmes and employee engagement frameworks.
- Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) / occupational health and safety risk — Operational hazards may affect employee safety and environmental performance. The BRSR material-issues table classifies Occupational health and safety as a risk with negative financial implications. Mitigation includes an occupational health and safety management system aligned with ISO 45001, a Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment procedure (SOP GSE024) and a Near Miss / Incident Reporting System (SOP GSE013), plus safety training and environmental management practices.
- Revenue concentration - single activity and heavy export dependence — The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from a single business activity (pharmaceutical research and development, manufacturing and marketing of complex injectables) and exports at 88.44% of total turnover, making the business structurally exposed to a single therapeutic-technology platform and to overseas regulatory, pricing and geopolitical conditions - in particular the U.S., which management identifies as the key momentum market. This concentration is disclosed in the BRSR but is not itself labelled as a risk by the Company.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Gland Pharma develops, manufactures and markets complex sterile injectables and generic injectable formulations, together with APIs, and provides contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) services to global pharmaceutical companies. Its portfolio spans liquid vials, lyophilised vials, pre-filled syringes, ampoules, infusion bags, ophthalmic products and cartridge-based delivery, serving oncology, ophthalmology, Central Nervous System (CNS) disorders and hospital critical-care segments. The company operates primarily on a business-to-business model with a specific focus on complex injectables, NCE-1s, First-to-File products and 505(b)(2) filings, and the 2023 acquisition of Cenexi localised manufacturing and development capability within Europe.

outlook.body:
- Expand the CDMO business and position Gland Pharma as the strategic partner of choice for global pharmaceutical companies seeking scalable injectable solutions, by integrating development expertise with manufacturing strength.
- Deepen specialisation in complex injectables - peptides, long-acting injectables, suspensions and hormonal therapies - as the source of competitive advantage and deeper market penetration.
- Build an expanding footprint in advanced drug delivery systems, specifically pens and cartridges, including the partnered GLP-1 platform.
- Continue expanding across both regulated and emerging markets to strengthen global presence and secure resilient revenue streams.
- Sustain targeted investment in R&D, complex injectables, drug-device combinations and co-development partnerships (R&D expenditure was ~5% of base business revenue in FY 2025-26) to build a differentiated pipeline.
- Pursue a differentiated pipeline spanning NCE generics, first-to-file opportunities and 505(b)(2) pathways.
- Leverage sterile injectable capability across 15+ therapeutic areas and 7 dosage forms as targeted diversification to strengthen market relevance in high-value segments.
- The Company states it is committed to driving superior value creation for all stakeholders, with the focus continuing to be future growth and the long-term interests of the Company and its shareholders; accordingly the Board 'would continue to adopt a progressive dividend policy, ensuring the immediate as well as long term needs of the business'. The Dividend Distribution Policy, framed under SEBI LODR and annexed to the Board's Report, lays down the criteria the Board considers before recommending a dividend, including ensuring the Company has sufficient distributable profits and/or general reserves as determined from a review of its audited financial statements prior to any declaration, and defines the form and time periods within which dividends are paid. Talent retention is supported through two Employee Stock Option Schemes (ESOP Scheme 2019 and ESOP Scheme 2025), administered by the ESOP Compensation Committee, with no changes made during the year. During the year the Company did not extend any loans or guarantees or make any investments covered under Section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013, other than an investment in its wholly owned subsidiary. There is no disclosed buyback, debt-reduction target or credit-rating commitment in the supplied text. The Company has no Associates or Joint Ventures during FY 2025-26.
- Occupational health and safety management system aligned with the ISO 45001 standard, supported by a Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment procedure (SOP GSE024) and a Near Miss / Incident Reporting System (SOP GSE013).
- National and international standards adopted and mapped to the NGRBC principles: ISO 45001:2018, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 9001:2015 and WHO GMP certificates.
- Replaced furnace oil with piped natural gas (PNG) as boiler fuel at all manufacturing facilities, stated to have significantly reduced stack emissions and lowered CO2 output.
- Bio-medical waste and wastewater management: effluent and sewage treatment plants at manufacturing facilities are regularly screened and upgraded, with strategies implemented for the treatment and recycling of wastewater.
- Water stewardship: significant improvements to the raw water underground storage tank and continual enhancement of the water quality sampling process, stated to have reduced overall water consumption.
- Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) applies and the waste collection plan is in line with the EPR plan submitted to Pollution Control Boards; packing waste goes to approved scrap vendors, e-waste to authorised recyclers and hazardous waste to State Pollution Control Board-approved TSDFs.
- FY 2025-26 disclosed environmental and safety outcomes (Key Highlights): 15.77% of energy derived from renewable sources, a 69.50% reduction in High Speed Diesel (HSD) oil consumption for steam generation, 2,969.85 MT of waste utilised and zero fatalities across manufacturing facilities.
- BRSR disclosures carry a Reasonable Level of Assurance from DNV Business Assurance India Private Limited.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion in FY 2025-26 is framed around two of the company's six strategic priorities - augmenting manufacturing capacities and capabilities, and the foray into complex CDMO including biologics. On capacity, the Company states it is commissioning additional manufacturing lines to support future growth across complex injectables and sophisticated delivery formats, scaling capacity through greenfield investments, and commissioning new production lines at the Pashamylaram facility for suspensions. Cartridge fill-and-finish capacity is being expanded to 140 million units per year; the GLP-1 platform note describes this as pen and cartridge capacity 'being scaled from ~40 million to 140 million units per year to meet anticipated demand growth', while the MD&A future-growth section states the Company has 'already expanded our cartridge fill-finish capabilities, from the present 40 Mn to 140 Mn' - the report is not internally consistent on whether the expansion is complete. The Company also states it is ramping up ophthalmic suspension capabilities and investing in technologies to extend CDMO capability across new modalities including biologics, drug substance and specialised formulations. In biologics CDMO, the Company entered a long-term strategic collaboration with Dr. Reddy's Laboratories at its biologics facility in Genome Valley, Hyderabad, collaborated with Shanghai Henlius Biotech to manufacture select biosimilar products, is expanding drug substance capabilities across monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and other biosimilars, and has secured CDMO contracts for complex products across suspensions, hormones, emulsions, peptides and microspheres plus eight GLP-1 programme contracts. Cenexi's Drug Product capabilities are being leveraged to offer integrated solutions alongside Gland manufacturing. Geographically, expansion is targeted at emerging markets across Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, APAC and Rest of the World, with recent forays into Saudi Arabia, China, South Africa, Mexico, Taiwan and South Korea. On the environmental side of capital spending, 2.15% of FY2026 capex went into technologies improving environmental and social impact - an effluent (Cyto/Non-Cyto) collection facility modified at Unit II and the VSEZ facilities - against 0.35% and 3.65% in FY2025 (effluent storage tank capacity enhancement, secondary containment pits, effluent segregation, a new RO plant, and solar rooftop project installations). No commissioning dates or completion timelines are given for any of the manufacturing projects.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global healthcare systems face sustained pressure to deliver both affordability and innovation, which management says makes a trusted, large-scale manufacturer of specialised injectables and a rapidly scaling CDMO partner increasingly crucial.
- Complex injectables are expected to remain a central pillar of growth, with more products being added to the pipeline.
- GLP-1 pen and cartridge capacity is being scaled to meet anticipated demand growth, following the partnered GLP-1 product Liraglutide being brought to the UK and Australia during the year.
- The Ready-to-Use (RTU) infusion bag portfolio addresses a market opportunity of approximately US$634 million in the U.S.
- Multiple CDMO contracts signed in GLP-1 and complex products are stated to provide clear medium-term revenue visibility.
- Growing focus on complex injectables is stated to enhance competitive advantage, enabling deeper market penetration, stronger partnerships and a resilient growth platform.
- Continued expansion across regulated and emerging markets is stated to strengthen global presence.
- Targeted investments in R&D, complex injectables, drug-device combinations and co-development partnerships are stated to drive a differentiated pipeline, accelerated regulatory momentum and stronger revenue visibility in regulated markets.
- Cumulative U.S. ANDA filings of 388, of which 337 are approved and 51 pending approval; 24 ANDAs filed and 28 approvals received in FY 2025-26.
- Ready-to-Use (RTU) infusion bag portfolio: 21 products filed, approval received for 18 so far, with an additional 11 currently under development.
- Co-development pipeline: 15 products advanced into co-development, comprising seven 505(b)(2) filings and eight ANDAs, with commercialisation expected from FY 2027-28 onwards.
- In-house complex pipeline: six products already launched and three more in line for approval.
- Strategic CDMO win: multiple contracts signed in GLP-1 and complex products, stated to provide clear medium-term revenue visibility.
- 36 molecules rolled out across regulated markets during FY 2025-26, including Colistimethate, Epinephrine, Dalbavancin, Liraglutide and Acetaminophen Bags.
- Base business: 30+ products launched, 15+ therapeutic areas covered, 7 dosage forms and 3 DMFs filed; Cenexi ~150 products and 90+ partners.

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q4FY26 performance driven by 22% revenue growth and 30% EBITDA margin, fueled by new product launches (Dalbavancin, Multivitamin) and CDMO expansion, with full-year EBITDA margin rising to 26% and Cenexi turning EBITDA-positive; what matters is the sustained margin expansion from high-value products and Cenexi’s path to mid-teens EBITDA, positioning Gland as a global complex injectables leader.

open.item: New prefilled syringe line at Herouville on track to be operational at the beginning of CY2026; two new lyophilizers at Braine-l'Alleud to be qualified by end of CY2025.
Biologics business (Dr. Reddy's) expected to contribute ~INR100 crores in FY26, gradually increasing thereafter.
CMS dry powder variation filings pending in European countries with approval expected in ~6 months, providing potential upside to guidance if faster.
Preparing to replace an old ampoule line at Fontenay this summer with a new high-capacity line adding 30 million ampoule capacity by 2027.
Dalbavancin (approved Feb, launched US and Europe) and multivitamin portfolio (approved April) expected to be meaningful contributors to growth in FY27 and beyond.
Management expects EBITDA margins to remain strong going forward, supported by high-end launches, product ramp-ups and CDMO execution.
Next-year (FY27) capex expected to be more than INR400 crores as part of the 5-year INR2,000 crore program.
15 products advanced into co-development (seven 505(b)(2) filings and eight ANDAs) are expected to commercialise from FY 2027-28 onwards.
The major CDMO (oncology) project announced earlier progressing well, expected to be commercialized in H2 FY28 with estimated annual revenue potential of USD25-30 million.
Reaffirmed capex outlay of INR2,000 crores over the next five years to fund capacity expansions for existing products and planned new launches.
Cenexi reaffirmed its mid-term objective of achieving a mid-teen EBITDA margin, supported by capacity increases and a fast-growing business pipeline.
Expand cartridge fill-and-finish capacity to 140 million units per year (from ~40 million) to capitalise on the GLP-1 opportunity.
The Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs 20 per equity share for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval.
An additional 11 Ready-to-Use (RTU) infusion bag products are currently under development, on top of 21 filed and 18 approved.
Three further in-house complex products are in line for approval, in addition to the six already launched.

open.horizon: at the earliest possible (no date stated)
open.item: Following the resignation of Chief Executive Officer Mr. Shyamakant Giri with effect from April 30, 2026, the Company states it will appoint a new Chief Executive Officer at the earliest possible.
Cenexi and Gland to increasingly operate as one unified platform, driving cross-selling and larger multi-geography contract wins.
Continuing to explore in-licensing opportunities in differentiated therapy areas and drug delivery systems like liposomals, biologics/biosimilars, plus capacity additions.
Cost initiatives (yield improvement, alternate sourcing, energy optimization, process efficiencies) continue to deliver approximately 1-2% margin improvement.
Commission new production lines at the Pashamylaram facility for suspensions.

verdicts.item: New oncology CDMO contract expected to commercialize in Q3/Q4 FY28 with ~$25-30 million annual revenue potential, requiring ~INR80 crores capex.
verdicts.note: 'One of the major CDMO projects announced earlier is progressing well and is expected to be commercialized in H2 of FY 28 with an estimated annual revenue potential of USD25 million to USD30 million.'…

verdicts.item: GLP-1 CDMO (two customers, three product contracts) expected to start showing some revenue in FY26.
verdicts.note: '8 contracts already signed and the additional 6 to 7 are expected to be signed soon'; but 'the guidance we give is excluding GLP... ramp-up will happen mostly' post-2030.

verdicts.item: New Pashamylaram capex lines (Bag line, Microsphere dry powder line, Hormones/Suspensions) to come onstream from next year, restoring Gland's old 2-2.5x asset turn.
verdicts.note: 'operating leverage with two additional lines getting commercialized'; new INR2,000cr brownfield with 'asset turn should be more than around 3x.' [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Cenexi FY25 revenue expected around EUR165 million, reaching EUR200 million next year (~0.8x asset turn), with 1x-2x asset turn over the medium term as new PFS/ampoule lines commercialize.
verdicts.note: FY26 Cenexi revenue EUR182m; 'FY 27, EUR200 million is the target we are looking at' - the EUR200m (originally next-year/FY26) pushed to FY27.

verdicts.item: Flagged delayed order pickup from Saudi Arabia (Enoxaparin) that is expected to start offtake by end of the quarter and lift H2 RoW revenue.
verdicts.note: 'Growth has been supported by tech-transfer and CDMO business, along with steady performance in our own portfolio' - RoW recovered, consistent with the Saudi Enoxaparin tech-transfer arrangement.

verdicts.item: Dalbavancin expected to launch in the US in the September quarter (Q2 FY26), a big US growth event, on track for approval and launch.
verdicts.note: 'we have received approvals, particularly Dalbavancin in February... Dalbavancin has been launched in U.S. and European markets and is already seeing strong demand' - delivered, though later than the …

verdicts.item: Cenexi EBITDA breakeven pushed from Q4 FY25 to Q3 FY26, driven by pushing top line to a ~EUR50 million per quarter run rate, following lost production from the ANSM Fontenay inspection.
verdicts.note: 'After a profitable Q3 FY 26 quarter... we delivered an EBITDA of EUR1 million in Q4 FY 26' - breakeven achieved and sustained. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed medium-term goal of delivering positive EBITDA in full year 2026, driven by pushing revenue beyond the EUR200 million threshold.
verdicts.note: 'returned to profitability for the 3 quarters during the year'; FY26 revenue EUR182m - positive but below the EUR200m threshold. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: 15 complex formulations under co-development with MAIA Pharmaceuticals (7 505(b)(2) and 8 ANDAs) with commercialization expected to begin from FY27.
verdicts.note: 'We also do co-develop projects, around 15 projects we are working with development partners' - the FY27 commercialization not specifically restated. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Cenexi targeted to reach high-teen EBITDA margins over the mid-to-long term (1-2 years).
verdicts.note: 'we are looking at mid-teen EBITDA level in the midterm'; FY27 target mid-single/high-single digit - approaching but below the original high-teen target.

verdicts.item: Guided GLP-1/cartridge fill-finish volumes to start at around 20 million units in FY27, ramping in subsequent years based on market approvals.
verdicts.note: 'the guidance we give is excluding GLP'; 'the ramp-up will happen mostly during that time' (post-2030) - the ~20m FY27 figure no longer emphasized. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: After a to-be-expected low Q2 FY26 (summer shutdown), Cenexi committed to deliver positive EBITDA in Q3 FY26, EBITDA-positive from October, ramping to low-teens/high single digits.
verdicts.note: 'After a profitable Q3 FY 26 quarter... we delivered an EBITDA of EUR1 million in Q4 FY 26, in line with our guidance.'

wtt.summary: 54% guidance hit (25 chains); 11/12 projects on-time; 23% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Highly confident; management reported highest-ever quarterly revenue/EBITDA and a completed Cenexi turnaround (positive EBITDA in 3 of 4 quarters), reaffirming strong forward margins and CDMO-led growth.
